options.opa: In both patients an increase of cytotoxic T lymphocytes will be detected.
options.opb: In both patients the innate immunity will be deficient.
options.opc: In both, an elevated level of serum IgE will be detected.

enhanced_information: Patients with helminth infections and those responding to allergens both exhibit an increased Th2 immune response, which is characterized by elevated levels of serum IgE. This is due to the activation of B cells to produce IgE in response to both helminth antigens and allergens. Therefore, the most accurate statement is that both conditions involve elevated serum IgE levels. While there may be some immune modulation in both cases, it does not necessarily imply a deficiency in innate immunity. Additionally, the risk of developing autoimmune diseases is not a common characteristic of either condition. Thus, the correct option is that both patients will have elevated serum IgE levels.
analysis: Both helminth infections and allergic responses are associated with elevated levels of serum IgE. Helminth infections often lead to a Th2 immune response, which is characterized by increased IgE production as part of the body's defense against parasitic infections. Similarly, allergic reactions also involve a Th2 response, resulting in elevated IgE levels in response to allergens. The other options do not accurately reflect common characteristics between these two conditions, as cytotoxic T lymphocytes are more involved in responses to viral infections and cancer, innate immunity is not necessarily deficient in these cases, and while there may be a predisposition to autoimmune diseases in helminth infections, it is not a common characteristic shared with allergic responses.
